external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty programme, mobile app, and partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: An application operated by another company that accesses the loyalty platform.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
external_entities.notes: The text refers to partner apps collectively; they are represented as one process and one external system type.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API; it keeps a refresh token on the phone.
processes.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app. The app signs a member in through our authorization server
processes.notes: The source says nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, handles authorization code flows, issues tokens, and manages partner consents.
processes.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and processes loyalty operations.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A web application operated by another company that can display a member's points and use the partner authorization flow.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
processes.notes: The text refers to partner apps collectively; each is represented by this process type.

processes.name: browser
processes.description: The browser used by a member to sign in, approve consent, and return an authorization code to a partner app.
processes.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member identity data, credentials, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: The source says nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.
data_flows.data_description: Member sign-in and authorization code flow messages

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API using an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: Rewards API requests carrying an access token

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests to the authorization server using its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: Token requests containing a client ID and client secret

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The browser is used to sign in on the authorization server and approve partner-app consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's registered redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and accesses member identity, authorization, token, and consent data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: update points ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes member balances and points transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write API logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request and its headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_flows.data_description: Requests received by the rewards API, including headers

data_flows.name: close member account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's cloud account where the described platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The member-controlled device zone where the mobile app and its refresh token are located.

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies that host partner apps.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member personal information, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the store contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member balances and points transactions, including gift-card-related loyalty data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the store holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because it stores request headers, which can include access-token credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request, headers included, is written to the store, while access tokens are used in API requests.
